proposals.before: Prognostication and observation drifted apart; the Directorate ordered Zhao Zhiwei to revise the Grand Clarity Calendar, and in eleven years the revision was done.
proposals.after: Prognostication and observation drifted apart; Zhao Zhiwei, Director of the Astronomical Directorate, was therefore ordered to revise the Grand Clarity Calendar, and in the eleventh year the calendar was completed.
proposals.reason: Chinese 命司天監趙知微 takes Zhao Zhiwei (with office title 司天監) as the person ordered, not the Directorate as agent; 十一年曆成 is the eleventh year, not a span of eleven years.

proposals.before: From this prognostication and observation drifted; therefore the Directorate ordered Zhao Zhiwei to revise the Grand Clarity Calendar—it was completed in the eleventh year.
proposals.after: From this prognostication and observation drifted; therefore Zhao Zhiwei, Director of the Astronomical Directorate, was ordered to revise the Grand Clarity Calendar—it was completed in the eleventh year.
proposals.reason: Chinese 命司天監趙知微 names Zhao Zhiwei with the title 司天監 as the object of 命; the Directorate is not the ordering agent.

proposals.before: Early in Mingchang the calendar office proposed yet another revision; Zhang Xingjian of the Rites Bureau said, "Wait for another solar eclipse, re-check until there is no discrepancy, and only then adopt it."
proposals.after: Early in Mingchang the calendar office proposed yet another revision; Zhang Xingjian, Director of the Ministry of Rites, said, "Please wait for another solar or lunar eclipse, re-check until there is no discrepancy, and only then adopt it."
proposals.reason: Chinese 日月食 means a solar or lunar eclipse, not solar only; 禮部郎中 is his office title, not a vague Rites Bureau affiliation.

proposals.before: Early Mingchang, the Directorate again reformed a new calendar; Zhang Xingjian, Director of Rites, said: "Please wait for another solar eclipse, re-verify without discrepancy, then use it."
proposals.after: Early Mingchang, the Directorate again reformed a new calendar; Zhang Xingjian, Director of Rites, said: "Please wait for another solar or lunar eclipse, re-verify without discrepancy, then use it."
proposals.reason: Chinese 日月食 covers sun or moon eclipse; rendering it as solar eclipse alone omits the lunar alternative.

proposals.before: Cover and subtract the day factor; the remainder is sunset fen.
proposals.after: Cover and subtract from the day factor; the remainder is sunset fen.
proposals.reason: 覆減日法 means subtract (sunrise fen) from the day factor; parallel s0257 correctly uses “from,” and the current wording leaves the minuend ambiguous.

proposals.before: Subtract sunrise fen by dusk-and-dawn fen for dawn fen; add to sunset fen for dusk fen.
proposals.after: Subtract dusk-and-dawn fen from sunrise fen for dawn fen; add to sunset fen for dusk fen.
proposals.reason: “Subtract A by B” is ungrammatical English and reverses the subtract-from relation that 以昏明分減日出分 states.

decisions.reason: s0014 has 禮部郎中張行簡 and 請俟他日月食; 日月食 covers solar or lunar eclipse, and 禮部郎中 is his office title, so the proposed idiomatic repair is accurate.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 禮部郎中張行簡言：「請俟他日月食，覆校無差，然後用之。」

decisions.reason: s0014 請俟他日月食 means wait for another solar or lunar eclipse; rendering only a solar eclipse omits the lunar alternative, and the proposed literal fix is accurate.
After s0249 yields sunrise fen, s0250 覆減日法 means subtract that result from the day factor; adding “from” correctly identifies the minuend and matches the remainder as sunset fen.
s0252 以昏明分減日出分 is subtract dusk-and-dawn fen from sunrise fen; “subtract sunrise fen by …” reverses the relation and is ungrammatical, so the proposed literal is required.
